newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs demand ban on female genital mutilation.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs demand ban on female genital mutilation.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday demanded an international ban on female genital mutilation, after an Egyptian court last month ruled the Cairo government could not outlaw the practice in public hospitals.

The EU assembly condemned the ancient practice, widespread in Africa and parts of the Middle East, as "torture" and slammed the court in Cairo for championing the radical Islamist cause against the government ban.

Euro-deputies urged the EU bloc to throw its weight behind a renewed United Nations campaign to eliminate female circumcision, which subjects some 130 million girls and women a year to usually very painful partial or total removal of external genital organs, or their mutilation.

It is carried out, sociologists say, largely to encourage the woman -- whose enjoyment of sexual relations is seriously impaired -- to remain a virgin until marriage and so be more attractive to a potential husband.
Medical experts say it very often leads to death through infection, or at least life-long health problems, as well as infertility and complications in giving birth.

In cultures where it is the accepted norm, mutilation is normally performed by traditional practitioners with crude instruments like knives, razors or broken glass, usually without anaesthetics, according to the World Health Organisation.
In more affluent groups, it may be performed in health clinics by qualified medical staff.

Reacting to concern in several EU countries -- especially France -- over the spread of female circumcision in immigrant communities, Euro-MPs said in a resolution that EU governments must severely prosecute anyone carrying out the practice.
